turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Come on through. Your partner says he'll wait outside unless you want him.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Leave him out there a minute, he fidgets. Um, I've been spotting, and I've got these cramps, and I'm pregnant, about eight to ten weeks. I'm really worried.
[SEG0003] person_1 (NURSE): Observations first. Blood pressure is 118 over 74, pulse 92, temperature 36.6.

[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): Is that pulse just nerves? My sister takes biotin every morning for her hair, great big tablets, she keeps on at me to start them and I nearly did, but I didn't. You're not meant to add random things. Sorry, I'm waffling.
[SEG0005] person_1 (NURSE): Oxygen saturation 98 percent. Doctor won't be long.
[SEG0006] person_3 (DOCTOR): Dr Ellison. Spotting and cramps. How many weeks are you?
[SEG0007] person_2 (PATIENT): Well, the last period was around Diwali, or after. So maybe eight weeks, maybe ten. I can't pin it.
[SEG0008] person_3 (DOCTOR): Heavy bleeding?
[SEG0009] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Spotting. Pink, then a bit brown. Not soaking a pad.
[SEG0010] person_3 (DOCTOR): Pain?
[SEG0011] person_2 (PATIENT): Low cramps, like a period, on and off. A couple of days, same as the spotting. Oh, and I take folic acid, 400 micrograms, once a day.
[SEG0012] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any shoulder-tip pain?
[SEG0013] person_2 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0014] person_3 (DOCTOR): Fainted at all?
[SEG0015] person_2 (PATIENT): No, I haven't fainted. I feel a bit washed out, that's all.
[SEG0016] person_3 (DOCTOR): Dizzy?
[SEG0017] person_2 (PATIENT): No, I don't think so.
[SEG0018] person_3 (DOCTOR): Fever?
[SEG0019] person_2 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0020] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any medicine allergies?
[SEG0021] person_2 (PATIENT): None.
[SEG0022] person_3 (DOCTOR): Do you smoke?
[SEG0023] person_2 (PATIENT): Never have.
[SEG0024] person_3 (DOCTOR): Alcohol?
[SEG0025] person_2 (PATIENT): I stopped when the test was positive. Not a drop since.
[SEG0026] person_3 (DOCTOR): Medical conditions? Previous pregnancies?
[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): No conditions. This is the first. We told my mum yesterday and she cried down the phone for ages, and the dog was sick on the rug in the middle of it, typical.
[SEG0028] person_3 (DOCTOR): Abdomen is soft, mild tenderness low down, no guarding.
[SEG0029] person_3 (DOCTOR): I'll book a routine scan for later this week. No blood tests today.
[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): Later this week? The cramps woke me at three. And this morning there was a small clot, not just spotting. I should've said that first.
[SEG0031] person_3 (DOCTOR): One clot?
[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes, a small one. And the cramp is sharper on the left now. Still not heavy, I'm not soaking anything.
[SEG0033] person_1 (NURSE): Sorry, her partner's asking if he can come in.
[SEG0034] person_3 (DOCTOR): Yes, send him in.
[SEG0035] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Sorry, I was pacing. She went really pale and woozy when she stood up this morning. She told me not to mention it.
[SEG0036] person_2 (PATIENT): I didn't faint. I just went light-headed for a minute, and it passed.
[SEG0037] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Alright. I've got my metformin in my pocket, 500 milligrams, for my diabetes, if we're stuck here. That's mine, not hers.
[SEG0038] person_3 (DOCTOR): Your metformin, understood. With the clot and the left-sided pain I'm changing the plan. Scan today, not next week, and bloods today as well.
[SEG0039] person_2 (PATIENT): Today? Oh, good. What bloods? My heart's been racing since yesterday, from the worry, not from running about. I barely slept.

[SEG0040] person_3 (DOCTOR): Pregnancy hormone, full blood count, and your blood group. Pelvic ultrasound this afternoon. This could be a threatened miscarriage, but I can't rule out an ectopic until the scan.
[SEG0041] person_2 (PATIENT): Will it hurt? My friend said the gel is freezing, and their waiting-room telly was stuck on an antiques programme the whole time.
[SEG0042] person_3 (DOCTOR): It shouldn't hurt. If the bleeding becomes heavy, or the pain is severe, or you feel faint, come straight back. Don't wait.
[SEG0043] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Even in the middle of the night?
[SEG0044] person_3 (DOCTOR): Yes. Early pregnancy unit, or A&E if it's out of hours.
[SEG0045] person_2 (PATIENT): And the folic acid, do I carry on?
[SEG0046] person_3 (DOCTOR): Yes. Keep taking it, 400 micrograms once a day.
[SEG0047] person_2 (PATIENT): What if the dates are completely wrong? There was a wedding the weekend after Diwali and I cannot remember if the period was before that or after. It's doing my head in.
[SEG0048] person_3 (DOCTOR): The scan will date the pregnancy. I can't fix the dates from that history.
[SEG0049] person_1 (NURSE): I can take the bloods now and book the scan for this afternoon.
[SEG0050] person_3 (DOCTOR): Both today. If the bleeding becomes heavy, or the pain is severe, or you feel faint, you come straight back, night or day.
[SEG0051] person_2 (PATIENT): Okay. I'm still really anxious, but alright, let's get it done.

doctor_changes_mind: the doctor says one plan, then changes it after new information; the label holds the final plan.

omissions.text: Negative finding asked and answered but not recorded: patient denied dizziness ('No, I don't think so'). This is later nuanced by the partner's report of wooziness/light-headedness on standing, but the direct denial of dizziness was omitted.
Bleeding detail not fully recorded: patient described the spotting as pink then a bit brown, and specifically said it was not soaking a pad / not soaking anything.
Symptom timing/detail not recorded: cramps had woken her at 3 a.m.
Positional/pallor detail of presyncope/light-headedness not recorded: partner reported she went really pale and woozy when she stood up this morning.

Plan change not recorded: the initial plan was a routine scan later this week with no blood tests that day, then this was changed to scan today and bloods today because of the clot and left-sided pain.
Follow-up timing advice not fully recorded: return night or day, including early pregnancy unit or A&E if out of hours, even in the middle of the night.
The family member's metformin 500 mg for diabetes was explicitly stated to be his, not the patient's. This should not be attributed to the patient.
